text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Finland's annual military spending will peak at 9.9 billion markka in the years 2002 and 2003 but the 2000-2008 average will be 9.5 billion markka, little changed from this year's 9.7 billion, according to plans in government security policy report.
- Wartime armed forces to fall to 430,000 soldiers from 540,000, according to government security policy report. @
- Cuts will not influence Finland's defence strength, says President Martti Ahtisaari.
- Finland plans to prohibit human cloning with a law restricting foster research.
- Still no government decision on postal services concession for Suomen Suoramainonta which applied for one two years ago.
- Being alone in very early childhood may cause depression or other mental imbalances later; long maternity leaves can even prevent adult schizophrenia, Finnish researchers say. @
- Police investigating smuggling of luxury cars via Finland to Russia.
- Helsinki region is again the country's economic engine, boosted particularly by private services activity.

- Rivals to introduce competitors to Nokia's 9000 Communicator which combines a mobile phone with a palmtop computer; smaller and cheaper solutions from Motorola and Sharp to enter the market in the autumn. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish pulp producers Enso and Metsa-Serla say they expect pulp prices to rise by 5-10 percent in May, and further hikes may be possible in the Autumn.
- National carrier Finnair's board to outline on Friday the basis for tenders to renew its 12 DC-9 planes and later all its 25 MD-80 aircraft.
- Money markets are vulnerable and prone to disturbances ahead of Economic and Monetary Union, warns finance ministry under-secretary of state Johnny Akerholm.
- Hundreds of companies are trying to redeem high interest rate loans from the state's regional investment fund Kera. @
- Sampo and other insurers are again interested in buying bankrupt Henki-Kansa as a result of rising real estate prices.

- Some international economists say they expect the Bank of Finland to raise its tender rate from 3.00 percent but Finnish analysts say there are no pressures for that and such talk is aimed at boosting foreign players' currency positions. @
AAMULEHTI

- President Martti Ahtisaari may have the chance to meet Presidents Boris Yeltsin and Bill Clinton separately during their Helsinki summit next week, though a meeting with Yeltsin has not been confirmed.
TURUN SANOMAT
- A book about the war in Bosnia written by a Finnish ex-mercenary may include valuable information for the war criminal tribunal in the Hague, says UN human rights envoy Elisabeth Rehn. @
DEMARI
- Finland faces no threats which would require membership in a military alliance, government security policy report says.
